ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors, and procurists against the Swiss Secretariat of State for Economic Affairs (SECO) sanctions lists, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Sanctions List, the US OFAC SDN List, and Swiss domestic criminal and terrorist financing watchlists. Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) due diligence is mandatory under AMLA Art. 3 and FINMA Circular 2016/7, including enhanced measures for foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates. Enhanced due diligence is required whenever a business relationship or transaction involves high-risk jurisdictions, cash-intensive activity, or complex cross-border structures; risk classification must be documented and updated.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix (Zentraler Firmenindex) operated by the Swiss Federal Statistical Office and the Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt (SHAB) / Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (FOSC); name clearance is executed through the cantonal commercial register office where the registered office of the AG will be situated.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Art. 950 of the Swiss Code of Obligations (OR), the company name may use Latin characters and shall be composed in German, French, Italian, or Romansh. A foreign-language name is admitted only where it is not misleading and is readily comprehensible to the Swiss public; any non-Latin or non-Swiss-script name must be transliterated into Latin script and, where necessary, accompanied by an explicit Swiss official-language descriptor identifying the legal entity form (e.g., 'Aktiengesellschaft AG' or 'Société Anonyme SA').
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the cantonal commercial register refuses a proposed name, the applicant may file a written objection with the same office within 10 days of the rejection notice, invoking the grounds under Art. 950 OR and the name-formation ordinances. If the objection is dismissed, a formal administrative appeal may be lodged with the competent cantonal administrative authority within 30 days of the dismissal. The last appellate remedy is an appeal to the Swiss Federal Administrative Court in St. Gallen under the Federal Administrative Procedure Act (Art. 44 et seq. of the Administrative Procedure Act, SR 172.021). For name reservation, a request for extension must be filed before expiry of the initial 30-day window; the cantonal register may grant one or more extensions where justification exists (e.g., pending notarial deed or apostille).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole statutory registered address for this business line. The ISIC 5630 specialty tea salon and lounge is a physical hospitality operation requiring a licensed operational site. Under Swiss and cantonal commerical-register practice, a virtual office may be used only as ancillary correspondence and administrative representation, while the AG must hold a physical lease and operating premises that satisfy cantonal hospitality and fire-safety regulations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated likelihood, approximately 75% within the first 12 months of operation. Because a specialty tea salon/lounge operates as a publicly accessible food-and-beverage establishment, cantonal health, fire safety, zoning, and commercial register authorities routinely conduct unannounced on-site inspections to verify physical presence, inventory, personnel, hygiene standards, and compliance with the hospitality license.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Articles 620–763 governing the Aktiengesellschaft; Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRA)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) acting with a licensed Swiss notary; public monitor: Zefix
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (Statuten), Commercial Register application form, and declaration by the incorporators
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital CHF 100,000; at least 20% (CHF 20,000) must be paid up before registration through a blocked bank account (Sperrkonto) in the company's founding name, released only after Commercial Register entry
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolved, acting as the founding board of [Company] Aktiengesellschaft, that the proposed share capital be and is hereby fully subscribed by the founders. Resolved that the initial paid-up portion of at least 20% shall be deposited into the blocked account at [Bank] and the account released only after commercial registration. Resolved that registered office is established at [Address], [Canton], Switzerland, and all necessary filings be executed. Resolved that [Name] serves as Chairperson, [Name] as Managing Director, and [Name] as Corporate Secretary. Resolved further that each officer and the notary are jointly authorized to sign and to complete incorporation pre-registration with the Commercial Register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) via a certified Swiss notary, in coordination with a FINMA-licensed bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Swiss notary to authenticate the Articles of Incorporation, confirm the legal form is AG, check company name availability in the Zefix index, and open a Swiss-franc blocked 'Sperrkonto' in the company's founding name. Deposit at least 20% of the minimum CHF 100,000 share capital, i.e., at least CHF 20,000, and obtain the bank's confirmation that the funds are blocked until Commercial Register registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (Statuten)
Founders' valid passports or identity cards
Written consents of designated board members and officers
Blocked account (Sperrkonto) confirmation from the bank
Business concept or intended corporate purpose statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the capital deposit or the notary identifies a defect in the founding documents, correct the documents or account naming and re-submit; the notary can issue a formal conformity declaration to cure the deficiency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton where the registered office will be located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, the notary submits the complete registration dossier to the Cantonal Commercial Register Office. The register verifies the legal name, capital coverage, corporate purpose, articles, and appointment of officers, and then enters the Aktiengesellschaft into the Commercial Register, thereby conferring legal personality.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Board members' and officers' written declarations of acceptance
Bank confirmation of the blocked paid-up capital
Commercial Register application and declaration form
Proof of the registered office address, such as a lease agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register office issues a deficiency notice, the notary submits amended or supplemental documents within 10 days; contested decisions can be appealed to the Cantonal Court of Appeal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in Swiss Official Gazette and UID Allocation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC) and Federal Statistical Office (BFS) for the UID register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon Commercial Register registration, the register automatically facilitates publication of the incorporation extract in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce. The Federal Statistical Office simultaneously issues the company's Swiss Business Identification Number (UID). The board must verify the UID and the published data through the Zefix online portal and update any discrepancies promptly.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract
Zefix identification number
UID number confirmation
Official gazette publication notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication contains inaccurate details, file a rectification request with the Commercial Register office within 30 days; any UID mismatch can be corrected through the UID Register Help Desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) and the competent Cantonal Tax Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the federal and cantonal corporate tax registration through the UID/Taxation Form (E1/TRI). Apply for Swiss VAT with ESTV if expected annual taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000; otherwise register voluntarily if the tea salon wishes to recover input VAT. File any required tax ruling with the cantonal tax administration to confirm taxable status and place of supply.
required_dossiers: UID confirmation
Commercial Register extract
Articles of Incorporation
Board resolution appointing tax representative if applicable
Estimated turnover form and financial plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax administration queries the application, resubmit the dossier with additional financial explanations through the ESTV secure portal; late registration may attract administrative fines but can be mitigated by corrective filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Cantonal and Municipal Food and Beverage Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Offices for Economic Affairs and Public Health (Gesundheitsdepartement) and municipal trade licensing authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application for the hospitality and food service permit (Bewilligung zum Betrieb einer Verpflegungsstätte); the tea salon is classified as a food service establishment under cantonal hospitality law. Undergo a food hygiene inspection by the cantonal food control authority, demonstrate compliance with the Swiss Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO) requirements, and obtain the municipal trade and safety clearances.
required_dossiers: Completed food and beverage license application form
Lease contract and floor plan of the tea salon
Certificate of food hygiene and allergen training
Municipal police and trade clearance
Employer liability and health insurance confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licensing authority issues a follow-up request, submit the missing documents within 20 working days; an adverse decision may be appealed to the Cantonal Administrative Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire Safety, Occupational Safety and Environmental Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Fire Safety Authority (Feuerpolizei), SUVA (Swiss National Accident Insurance), and Cantonal Environmental Protection Office (Amt für Umwelt)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a fire safety certificate after inspection of the tea salon premises, verifying escape routes, alarms, and fire extinguisher readiness. Ensure structural load capacity through the building inspection certificate. File occupational health and safety documentation with SUVA and register employees with the compensation fund. Submit the simplified environmental registration confirming no hazardous industrial emissions and compliance with local wastewater and waste handling ordinances.
required_dossiers: Fire safety inspection certificate
Building and structural load verification
Workplace safety declaration submitted to SUVA
Waste and wastewater registration form
Environmental compliance declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the environmental agency requires a higher category, submit a remediation or facility-specific action plan; if fire safety defects are noted, correct the structural or equipment failures and request re-inspection through the Fire Safety Office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Trade and Industry Office (Gewerbe- und Industrieamt) jointly with the Municipal Trade Permit Authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Bewilligung zum Betrieb einer Gastwirtschaft / Gastgewerbsbewilligung (Restaurant and Tea Lounge Operating Permit)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) and Cantonal Environmental Protection Office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full Environmental Impact Assessment; subject to simplified registration because a specialty tea salon lounge does not constitute a hazardous-emission industrial facility under Annex 2 of the Swiss EIA Ordinance.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with the Swiss Water Protection Act (GSchG) and cantonal sewer ordinances; volatile organic compounds from cleaning and preparation processes must remain below LRV (Swiss Clean Air Ordinance) thresholds; waste must be separated and disposed of in accordance with the Swiss Federal Waste Ordinance (BUD).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the cantonal fire police; structural load inspection and building certification; occupational health and safety compliance with SUVA; workplace safety and civil defense shelter designation assessed for the registered premises.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB; Schweizerische Nationalbank, Banque nationale suisse, Banca nazionale svizzera), located in Bern and Zurich, operating under the Federal Act on the Swiss National Bank and the Federal Act on Currency and Legal Tender; the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) is the licensing and AML supervisory counterpart.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland operates a fully liberalised foreign-exchange regime. The Swiss franc is freely convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions. There are no exchange controls, no prior permit for capital inflows or outflows, no restrictions on profit remittance, loan repayment, or share-capital repatriation for non-resident shareholders. The only applicable formalities are the statutory 35% anticipatory withholding tax on dividends (reclaimable or reduced under double taxation treaties), CRS/FATCA reporting obligations for non-resident account holders, and SNB balance-of-payments statistics reported indirectly by the mandated bank. Sectoral restrictions such as the Lex Koller on real estate acquisitions do not affect a specialty tea-salon trade operation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Swiss law imposes no mandatory surrender, no statutory conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline for export proceeds. Exporters may hold receipts indefinitely in any convertible currency, onshore or offshore. Cross-border payment data is aggregated by banks for SNB statistical reporting, but individual treasury decisions are unrestricted.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto) / Operational Current Account in CHF, EUR, USD
Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto) / Operational Current Account with SEPA and SWIFT access
Operational Current Account in CHF and EUR; capital confirmation available subject to domicile relationship
Operational Current Account in CHF; limited multi-currency treasury services
Operational Current Account only; standard retail-oriented corporate services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as an ancillary settlement channel, Low as the primary treasury relationship. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Revolut Business, Payoneer) may support low-balance merchant settlements and small cross-border supplier payments, but they cannot issue the mandatory capital confirmation for a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft, cannot hold the statutory blocked share-capital escrow, and are not a substitute for a licensed Swiss bank under the Federal Act on Banks. Deposit-taking from Swiss-resident customers without a banking or FinTech licence (Art. 1, 1a, 1b Banking Act) is prohibited; unlicensed cross-border deposit-taking is a criminal offence enforceable by FINMA. Recommended structure: principal banking at UBS Switzerland AG or ZKB, plus a controlled EMI float strictly for payment-card settlement under an explicit internal treasury policy.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated AG, at least one authorised signatory and the ultimate beneficial owner must undergo a physical KYC interview at the Swiss bank branch. Fully remote opening is generally permitted only if the director is a Swiss/EU/EEA passport holder and uses a FINMA-approved video-identification process in accordance with FINMA Circular 2016/07. Non-EU/EEA directors require in-person identity verification, notarised and apostilled documents, certified translations, and an original board resolution approving the account opening. The bank will additionally require a lease agreement for the salon premises, a commercial register excerpt, and a plausible business plan. A capital escrow account cannot be opened on a purely offshore remote basis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership or nominee-shareholder pattern on the AG register
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified commercial register excerpt, complete Art. 9 AMLO beneficial-owner declaration, ownership-chain organisational chart, passport and proof-of-address for all UBOs, apostilled board resolution, and a source-of-funds statement covering the CHF 100,000 share capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive retail receipts inconsistent with declared high-end tea-salon turnover
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified POS terminal contracts, cash-management policy with daily till reconciliation, audited or Swiss-certified accountant financial projections, the salon lease agreement, Zefix excerpt, and Swiss VAT (MWST) registration confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wires from or to high-risk tea and ceramic supplier jurisdictions without underlying documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed supplier purchase contracts, commercial invoices with ISIC-compatible descriptions, shipping documents (bills of lading, air waybills), Swiss customs declarations, insurance certificates, and the full correspondence trail for the specific SWIFT gpi / MT103 reference.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP screening hits on a director or UBO name
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal PEP and sanctions screening results from a FINMA-recognised data provider, official identification documents showing full name, date of birth, and nationality, a legal opinion confirming no nexus to sanctioned persons, and proactive disclosure of any political-exposure status in the KYC questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained settlement volatility from EMI or payment-platform inflows (e.g., Stripe, Adyen, PayPal)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant settlement reports, platform payout logs, transaction-level POS and card records, daily sales reconciliation notes, an internal netting calculation, and annual statutory auditor verification of the treasury ledger.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders remit the CHF 100,000 minimum share capital (at least CHF 50,000 paid-in at incorporation, per Art. 632 para. 2 of the Swiss Code of Obligations) via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Credit Transfer to a bank-designated blocked capital account (Sperrkonto), referencing 'Capital Contribution - Einlagezahlung' and the company registration name. The bank issues a formal capital confirmation (Bankenbestätigung) attesting that the funds are paid in and will be at the free disposal of the board upon commercial register registration. Foreign-currency remittances must be explicitly converted to CHF at an agreed spot rate, with the SWIFT narrative showing the original currency, conversion rate, and resulting CHF amount. No capital import permit, FDI registration, or settlement approval is required. The account is then unblocked and converted into the operational treasury account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For high-value tea and ceramic imports: SWIFT MT103 with gpi tracking for correspondent-bank settlement; irrevocable confirmed documentary commercial letters of credit (UCP600) for primary shipments from India, China, and East Asia; documentary collections (D/P forms) for lower-value consignments; SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant for EU suppliers; and SWIFT MT202/MT300 for interbank liquidity alignment. All outbound invoices must include the Swiss UID and VAT number and HS codes for tea (HS 0902) and ceramics; no exchange-control approval is required. Payment narratives must match the commercial accrual and pass bank AML reasonableness checks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (EUR/CHF, USD/CHF, GBP/CHF, and CNH/CHF up to 12-month tenors) under ISDA or a bank's standard FX master agreement
FX Swaps for short-term rollover of cross-border supplier liquidity
Cross-currency swaps (CHF against EUR or USD) for capital expenditure or term financing
Plain-vanilla FX options and zero-premium collars on forecast import disbursements

Non-deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on supplier-market currencies such as INR or IDR, permissible as economic hedges, but not standard onshore against CHF given full CHF deliverability; if offered, they require an interbank back-to-back booking and additional credit-limit approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and statutory audit report (ordinary audit cases) — commercial register filing and SHAB publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt) at the registered seat; publication through Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after balance-sheet date (AGM deadline for calendar-year AGs: 30 June); if the AG has ordinary audit, the commercial register filing follows the AGM and is customarily accomplished before the end of the subsequent year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Commercial register authority issues a default notice; further non-compliance exposes directors to disciplinary fines and the commercial register court may order judicial dissolution of the AG

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss direct federal and cantonal corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration of the registered office, with Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) coordination for the direct federal portion
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Cantonal filing calendar; calendar-year corporate taxpayers are commonly required to file between 31 March and 30 June of the following tax year, with one or more extensions available up to 30 September
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Discretionary tax assessment, late-payment interest, administrative penalty up to 50%-100% of omitted tax, and criminal sanctions in cases of intentional tax evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss Value Added Tax return (quarterly, semi-annual, or annual depending on taxable turnover)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 60 days after the end of the reporting period; for annual declarants this falls on or about 28/29 February of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest, penalty up to 50% of the additional tax due, default assessment by ESTV, and criminal prosecution for repeated intentional non-declaration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AHV/AVS annual employer wage statement and contribution declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal or private AHV/AVS compensation office (Ausgleichskasse) designated by the employer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before 31 January following the wage year; final contribution payment and wage statement due on the same date unless the compensation office grants an extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest, administrative surcharge, personal liability of directors, and penal proceedings for failure to pay AHV contributions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Board certification of the share register and beneficial-owner information before the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General shareholders' meeting; annual minutes retained in the company's statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At the annual shareholders' meeting, which must be held within six months after the balance-sheet date (calendar-year AG: by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of voting rights for unregistered transfers, board liability for inaccurate registers, and possible forced registration procedures through court order

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary independent audit is compulsory for an AG if it is a listed or public-bond issuer, if it must produce consolidated financial statements, or if for two consecutive years it exceeds two of: CHF 20 million balance-sheet total; CHF 40 million net turnover; 250 full-time-equivalent employees. All other AGs are subject to limited audit unless the company has no more than 10 FTE and all shareholders expressly waive the audit for the relevant annual period.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR, Art. 957-963b) as local GAAP; Swiss GAAP FER is accepted as a supplementary standard; IFRS Accounting Standards are available and required where the AG is listed or produces consolidated accounts under specified rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual Swiss UBO registry filing is required. For registered shares, the board must enter each transfer in the share register before the acquirer can be treated as a shareholder; on each transfer the board obtains and records the beneficial-owner identification. Before the annual general meeting, the board reviews and confirms the completeness of the share register, and this confirmation forms part of the meeting minutes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (board minutes and director-list records)
Minute Book of General Meetings and board resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,100 - 3,300 (CHF 1,000 - 3,000) per annum, depending on canton and registered-agent provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - 13,000 for a limited audit/review of the specialty-tea AG; USD 13,000 - 45,000 for an ordinary statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal CIT; combined cantonal Zug statutory rate 14.83% (2024)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays; notable preferential regimes: (i) patent box in Zug (up to 90% exemption on qualifying IP-derived income); (ii) R&D super-deduction (additional 50% deduction in certain cantons); (iii) participation exemption (100% relief on qualifying dividends and capital gains from substantial shareholdings of ≥10%); (iv) transitional measures only for legacy domiciliary companies abolished after 2020 tax reform.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Steuererklärung juristische Personen (Corporate Tax Return for Legal Entities); e-filing through the canton Zug Tax Portal (TaxMe/e-tax) and Swiss Confederation's secure electronic submission system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., 31 December year-end due 30 June of the following year; extension to 31 October available upon application).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, UID number, registered seat, legal form (Aktiengesellschaft), principal activity (specialty tea salon and lounge operations).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not required to file Swiss tax returns; the Swiss entity must list its domiciliary address and local place of administration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue and net profit from tea sales, lounge service, cultural events, and retail merchandise; includes turnover from all Swiss payment rails (POS, credit card).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income attributable to the Swiss activity; foreign parent entities making independent sales are not aggregated unless a Swiss permanent establishment exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: raw tea leaves, rent, salaries, depreciation on ceramic ware and furniture, marketing, bank charges, and professional fees, with substantiating documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border charges (intercompany management fees, royalties, interest) must not be deducted unless supported by transfer-pricing documentation and arm's-length pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D – Adjustments, Losses and Tax Credits (Box 30-40)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory adjustments, carry-forward losses (7-year limit), patent box deduction, participation exemption claims, and any Swiss withholding tax reclaims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot claim Swiss tax credits on the entity's profits; the Swiss entity may reclaim withheld tax on its own dividend income where treaty or domestic law provides relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: reminder fee up to CHF 100; procedural fine (Ordnungsbusse) up to CHF 10,000 per tax year; late-payment interest of 3%–5% per annum; deliberate omission constitutes tax evasion subject to fines up to 100% of evaded tax and criminal penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on gross dividends distributed by a Swiss AG; under the participation exemption the 35% rate is reduced to 0% for qualifying group dividends (≥10% shareholding and holding period ≥1 year); DTA rates for non-residents generally range 0%–15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident beneficial owners must obtain a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from their home tax authority and file a refund claim with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA) using Form 824 (individuals) or Form 850 (companies). These forms require account details, shareholding evidence, and a declaration of beneficial ownership; the claim must be filed within three years of the dividend payment. Where a relief-at-source arrangement has been approved, the paying agent may apply treaty rates at the time of distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: 0% withholding tax on royalties and interest. Treaty rates: generally 0% for copyright/patent royalties and business interest in most Swiss DTAs; some DTA variants impose 5% on industrial equipment royalties; interest in nearly all treaties is 0%. No Swiss WHT relief procedure is required because no tax is triggered.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss law does not impose statutory local-file monetary thresholds; in practice the tax administration orders contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation when cross-border related-party transactions exceed CHF 500,000 per annum. A CbC report is mandatory for MNE groups with consolidated revenue of at least CHF 900 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no separate ESR regime (unlike UAE). Economic substance is nonetheless assessed through Swiss GAAR and treaty anti-abuse provisions; taxpayers must demonstrate local management, physical premises, real staff, and commercial purpose to retain treaty and participation benefits. Shell or mailbox companies are blocked, and the principal-purposes test (PPT) under the MLI may deny DTA relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting inaccurate or incomplete tax declarations, suppressing cash sales in the tea salon, fabricating vendor invoices for tea inventories or décor, and failing to report `E-commerce / POS / credit-card revenue`.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional payment up to 100% of evaded tax plus interest; procedural fines up to CHF 10,000; aggravated fraud (e.g., forging records) carries imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to CHF 250,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false returns are civilly jointly liable for unpaid taxes and penalties; criminal conviction triggers personal fines, travel bans, extradition risks, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal address in Zug with no real office, no local personnel, or no substantive beverage/cultural activity while claiming Swiss residency benefits or treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, participation exemption, and patent box; retroactive re-assessment of taxable income; fines up to the tax advantage; potential deregistration by the commercial register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal liability for the tax adjustments if they implement a sham structure; travel bans and imprisonment can be imposed in cases of intentional fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering via Payment Processing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting repeated cash payments exceeding CHF 15,000 without identification, structuring transactions to avoid reporting, creating false credit-card settlement records to disguise illicit funds, or failing to identify beneficial owners of premium bulk tea purchases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Art. 305bis of the Swiss Criminal Code: imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine up to CHF 500,000; confiscation of laundered assets; violation of the Swiss AML ordinance (SRO) can trigger license revocation and strengthened oversight.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors acting as compliance/de facto AML officers may be prosecuted personally; civil restitution, court-imposed travel bans, prohibition from serving as board members, and imprisonment are all available.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border management fees, trademark royalties, or intercompany loans not meeting arm's-length terms, with no contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation; high-margin tea imports from related suppliers without benchmark studies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer-pricing adjustment increasing taxable profits; interest at 5% per annum; penalty of up to 30% of the deficiency in negligent cases and up to 100% for wilful evasion; CbC or OECD exchange of information automatically flagged.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Financial directors and responsible officers are personally liable for false documentation; intentional TP fraud can lead to criminal fines and imprisonment up to 5 years, plus personal claims for restitution.
